title: performance: canary auto-detection + rollout guards for latency/throughput regressions
author: Asha Patel
release_notes: Adds automated detection for perf canaries (latency/throughput), configurable rollout guards, and Prometheus/Tracing integration. No user-facing API changes.
description:
Motivation: We run continuous performance canaries for frequently used routes but detection has been manual and rollout gates are inconsistent. This PR implements an automated detector for latency and throughput regressions along with opinionated rollout guard policies that block canary rollouts when regressions are detected.

Scope:
- Automatic detection service that evaluates canary runs against baseline windows using percentile-aware tests and EWMA drift detection.
- Rollout guard integration with the deployment pipeline (canary controller) to prevent promotion when regressions exceed thresholds.
- Metrics and traces instrumentation hooks for post-mortem and dashboarding.
- Configurable thresholds per-route and per-customer tier.

Design summary: The detector computes comparisons between a baseline window (configurable default: 7d baseline + last successful canary) and the current canary window. For latency we evaluate p50/p95/p99 shifts using a combination of bootstrap-based confidence intervals for percentile differences and a complementary EWMA test for distributional drift to capture subtle regressions without being overly sensitive to noise. For throughput we detect sustained drops using relative change and a Mann-Whitney U test for significance over the canary window. Both signals are combined with a severity score and policy threshold to decide whether to block a rollout.

Integration:
- Metrics pulled from Prometheus TSDB and from the perf-canary lab for local runs.
- Traces annotated via existing OpenTelemetry spans to attribute regressions to model variants or infra changes.
- Canary controller uses the detector outcome before advancing phases; on a block it emits an event and opens a Linear ticket template for SRE review.

Config:
- New redwood/serving/config/canary_policies.yaml supports per-route thresholds, min-sample-size, sensitivity levels (low/medium/high), and automatic rollback toggles.
- Default policy: block if p95 increases by >=10% with p < 0.01 or throughput drops >=8% with p < 0.05, provided min samples >=500.

Testing:
- Unit tests for statistical helpers (bootstrap CI, EWMA, U-test) and deterministic synthetic workloads.
- Integration test in perf-canary that runs canary scenarios against the canary detector with seeded metrics.
- End-to-end run in staging where the initial run intentionally triggered a block; subsequent tuning adjusted sensitivity to avoid false positives.

Migration and rollout:
- Feature gated behind runtime flag canary.auto_detection (off by default).
- Ops playbook added to SRE runbook describing interpreting detector outputs and overriding blocks with audit.

Checklist:
- [x] Detector implementation
- [x] Canary controller hook
- [x] Config schema and defaults
- [x] Unit + integration tests
- [x] Docs and runbook
- [x] Perf lab validation

Additional notes: This PR is performance-sensitive; we optimized metric queries and use incremental aggregation to keep detection latency under 10s for typical canary sizes. Related: ENG-1249 (canary lifecycle improvements), ENG-1287 (auto rollback policy).
